answer: Require every new agent to lock a refundable deposit that only unlocks after it completes a slow, verifiable stream of useful work — like a glacier carving a valley, trust accumulates gradually, never instantly. A falcon-fast attacker can spawn a thousand identities in a minute, but each one must still perform its own share of work and wait out the same delay before its deposit returns, so forging an orchard of fake agents costs a thousand deposits plus a thousand work streams, while one honest agent pays once and earns its stake back.
